_comment: Accepted Slither results (SECURITY-CI.md, 'Accepting a finding'). fingerprint (contrib/slither/gate.py: check + elements' names and files, no line numbers) -> {check, where, reason, by, date}. Every entry needs a reason a reviewer can check. Re-triage when the flagged code changes (the fingerprint then changes and the result re-opens).

d8208d21e21f90b7.reason: `id == 0 || id != proposalId` compares a stored proposal id with the one the challenger signed; strict equality is the point (a challenge binds one proposal). The detector targets balance checks; no balance is involved.

6d85dab37e646a92.reason: `block.timestamp / capWindow == mintWindow` compares two window indices (integers); equality is exact by construction, no balance is involved. View function.

a645bc6a75d370d2.reason: `w == mintWindow` compares the current rate-limit window index with the stored one; equality is the intended same-window test, no balance is involved.

58d2edef418ef008.reason: `address p` is assigned in the try branch and the catch branch reverts, so it is always set before use; Slither does not model try/catch.

d30e65cc1f2da437.reason: The external call is to the immutable `token` (WrappedYcash: stock OpenZeppelin ERC-20, no hooks or callbacks); it cannot re-enter. burnNonce++ after the call is safe.

655ad311acbc5fb1.reason: Event after the call to the immutable, hook-free `token`; no re-entry is possible, so event order is fixed.

e80fc54444bcc58b.reason: Event after token.crosschainMint on the immutable, hook-free `token`; consumed[lockId] and the rate limit are written before the call (checks-effects-interactions).

8425b2632f2f666d.reason: The flagged comparison is of proposal ids, not of a timestamp (Slither taints it through the Proposal struct that also holds eta).

7221e46e4a8b437c.reason: `block.timestamp < p.eta`: the challenge window is >= 2 hours on mainnet (MIN_MAINNET_CHALLENGE_WINDOW); validator timestamp skew is seconds. Design §4.5.3.

ef21f4ed28b95beb.reason: View-only mirror of executeMint's eta check; same reasoning (window of hours, skew of seconds).

876b76733e430f13.reason: Rate-limit windows are `block.timestamp / capWindow`, capWindow in hours/days; a few seconds of skew moves a window boundary by seconds at most. View function.

15c651d4ee3e7b9f.reason: Same fixed-window rate limit as mintAvailable; skew of seconds against windows of hours does not change the bound materially (design §4.5).
